skill.name: github-code-review
skill.description: Coordinate GitHub pull request reviews with ruv-swarm agents, GitHub CLI workflows, and CI review automation.
skill.summary: Run multi-agent GitHub pull request reviews across security, performance, style, architecture, and accessibility.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: The Markdown-only skill mostly contains documentation and examples, and many static backtick findings are false positives from code fences. Real risks remain where the skill instructs agents or CI to run gh, npx, and execSync, especially webhook comment handling, GitHub token use, and automated PR approval or merge actions.

remediation.issue: Webhook comment commands reach execSync without validation in the sample handler.
remediation.suggestion: Verify GitHub webhook signatures, authorize commenters, allowlist commands, and use spawn or execFile with argument arrays instead of shell strings.

remediation.issue: CI examples use GITHUB_TOKEN for review automation and repository-changing commands.
remediation.suggestion: Scope tokens to the minimum permissions, separate read-only review from write actions, and avoid exposing token-backed command output in logs.

remediation.issue: Examples can approve or auto-merge pull requests based on automated output.
remediation.suggestion: Require branch protection, human approval, and explicit policy checks before approval, merge, labels, or generated fixes are applied.

remediation.issue: Many examples run npx ruv-swarm directly against pull request data.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, document trusted installation sources, and require confirmation before running networked CLI commands on repository content.

static_findings.snippet: run: echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | gh auth login --with-token
- ✅ Cache analysis results to avoid redundant work

finding_verdicts.reason: The sample webhook imports child_process and later uses it for shell execution. This is a real risk if copied into automation without strict validation.
execSync runs npx ruv-swarm from GitHub webhook data. Even though the PR number is expected to be numeric, it creates server-side command execution risk.
execSync builds a shell command from a PR comment body. Untrusted comments can influence command arguments, creating command injection risk.

content.user_title: Review GitHub Pull Requests with AI Agents
content.value_statement: Manual pull request review can miss security, performance, and architecture issues. This skill coordinates specialized review agents and GitHub workflows for structured review coverage.
actual_capabilities: Initializes ruv-swarm review workflows from GitHub pull request context.
Runs specialized review flows for security, performance, architecture, style, and accessibility.
Posts pull request comments, labels, and review decisions through GitHub CLI examples.
Defines CI workflow examples for automated review and quality gates.
Shows patterns for custom review agents and cross-PR analysis.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI, repository access, and ruv-swarm tooling to run the examples.
Automated findings still need human verification before merge decisions.
Some examples require careful token scoping and webhook validation before production use.
It does not guarantee detection of every vulnerability or regression.

use_cases.title: Review Security-Sensitive Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Run focused review agents for authentication, authorization, secrets, and dependency risks before requesting approval.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Pull Request Reviews
use_cases.description: Apply consistent review criteria for style, tests, architecture, and accessibility across a repository.

use_cases.title: Add Review Automation to CI
use_cases.description: Build GitHub Actions workflows that gather PR context, run review agents, and publish review summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic PR Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review pull request 123. Summarize changed files, likely risks, and the first review commands to run.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 for security issues. Focus on authentication, authorization, secrets, dependencies, and unsafe input handling.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CI Review Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions review workflow for this repository. Include quality gates for security, tests, coverage, and architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Advanced Multi-Agent Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Large pull request or release review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a comprehensive review plan for pull request 123 with security, performance, architecture, style, and accessibility agents. Include merge criteria.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that changes authentication and session handling.
output_examples.output: The review plan assigns security and architecture agents first. Expected output includes risk summaries, requested tests, and approval blockers.

output_examples.input: Add automated review to a repository CI pipeline.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a workflow that collects PR context, runs ruv-swarm review commands, posts a summary, and applies labels.

output_examples.input: Generate comments for a large refactor pull request.
output_examples.output: The skill groups findings by file, severity, and agent type so maintainers can prioritize fixes before approval.

best_practices: Use least-privilege GitHub tokens and verify webhook signatures before enabling automation.
Review automated comments before approving, merging, or pushing generated fixes.
Start with read-only review workflows before enabling labels, approvals, or auto-fixes.
anti_patterns: Do not execute PR comment commands without validating the commenter and command allowlist.
Do not expose GitHub tokens, diffs, or review output in public logs.
Do not use automated approval or merge flows without branch protection and human oversight.

faq.question: What tools does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects GitHub CLI, npx, ruv-swarm, and repository permissions for the target pull request.

faq.question: Can it replace human code review?
faq.answer: No. It structures review coverage and produces findings, but maintainers should verify results before approval.

faq.question: Does it support security review?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes security review flows for OWASP issues, secrets, permissions, dependencies, and critical blockers.

faq.question: Can it post GitHub comments?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show GitHub CLI commands for comments, inline review feedback, labels, and review states.

faq.question: Is CI automation included?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes GitHub Actions examples for automated review, quality gates, and status updates.

faq.question: What permissions should I use?
faq.answer: Use the minimum repository permissions required, scoped tokens, webhook signature checks, and branch protection rules.
